title: The Tripling Frost Moths
story: High on the Glacier Stair, Mr 6 meets Velmora, a single pale moth whose wings shed freezing dust. Every time a sword touches her, she bursts into three moths — and each of those will triple again at the next strike. 'Swing away, little digit,' she shimmers. Mr 6 sheathes his sword and counts instead.
question: Velmora starts as 1 moth and triples with each strike. If a knight strikes her 4 times, and then Mr 6's warming lantern melts away 27 of the moths, how many moths are left?
praise: Tracking the tripling all the way to 81 was the hard part — the lantern's 27 just needed to be subtracted at the end.
hint: Triple one step at a time: 1, 3, 9, ... and only subtract after all four strikes.
victory: Mr 6 held up the lantern and said, 'You're 54 now — too many to agree on anything.' The moths argued, scattered, and settled into the warm light as a very confused glittering blanket.
imagePrompt: A caped numeral-six knight raises a glowing warm lantern on an icy glacier staircase as dozens of pale frost moths swirl in cold blue moonlight.
